turns.reply: The regex's ASCII range stops at `\u006f` ('o'), so most lowercase letters and `{|}~` miss the fast path. The intended range is printable ASCII, up to `\u007e`. Fixing that.

turns.reply:
The fix is in `rich/cells.py`: the single-cell-width fast-path regex stopped its printable-ASCII range at `\u006f` ('o'), so characters like lowercase letters after 'o', `{`, `|`, `}` and `~` fell off the fast path. I changed the range to end at `\u007e` and submitted a one-line patch.

I checked it with a quick inline script: `cell_len('hello world')` returns 11, `set_cell_size` pads correctly, and the regex matches `~{}` while rejecting a CJK character. I did not run the repository's test file.
